title: Vector distance sanity layer and client-tolerant similarity mode
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem statement: clients and stored vector collections across customers currently mix two semantics for similarity scoring: raw dot-product on unnormalized vectors, and cosine-style comparisons that assume normalized vectors. Inconsistencies cause subtle quality regressions for reranking, skewed unit economics (token/compute per query), and operational surprises when we change serving knobs (quantization, kernel selection, batching). We need a runtime-level, low-latency 'sanity layer' that enforces a consistent distance contract while remaining tolerant of legacy clients and persisted vector corpora. The goal is to guarantee correct scoring semantics (cosine vs dot) per request, provide a clear compatibility/rollback path, and reduce client breakage while keeping tail latency and cost within SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts an explicit similarity mode header (X-Embed-Similarity-Mode) with values: legacy-dot, cosine, auto
When header is not provided, runtime behaves in default backward-compatible mode (legacy-dot) for flagged tenant cohorts and 'auto' for new tenants

Server exposes a lightweight normalization adapter that can: re-normalize incoming vectors on-the-fly, detect stored vector norm distribution for a customer, and apply per-request scoring policy without copying full datasets
End-to-end latency increase is <= 5ms p95 on typical reranker traffic for the canary config
Quality regression for existing customers is minimized; migration experiments show no >1.5% drop in rerank NDCG@10 when running default compatibility mode
Comprehensive unit+integration tests for dot vs cosine implemented and run in CI; synthetic fuzz tests included
Migration tooling to export a customer's stored vectors with normalized values is provided and documented
Developer docs and SDK additions for Python/Node describing header, parameter, and recommended migration steps are published
Dashboard with per-tenant similarity-mode telemetry and drift alarms is available before full rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — design & spec: finalize API header and runtime contracts; collect stakeholder sign-off (PM, SDK, docs)
Phase 1 — internal runtime shim: implement normalization adapter behind feature flag; unit/integration tests; perf microbenchmarks
Phase 2 — canary: enable shim for 1% of traffic on non-critical tenants; monitor latency, cost, and NDCG regression metrics; 72-hour stability window
Phase 3 — tenant opt-in: SDK exposes opt-in header (cosine) and monitoring; onboarding docs for customers with high-quality sensitivity
Phase 4 — selective migration: provide re-normalization export tool and guide; assist customers on request
Phase 5 — evaluation: after 2 quarters of opt-ins, consider switching default for new tenants to 'auto' or 'cosine' if metrics justify
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring operator with both normalized and unnormalized vectors
Integration tests that simulate stored vectors with mixed norms and verify consistent results when using header-based mode
Load tests exercising batching + normalization adapter to measure CPU/memory overhead per 1k QPS
A/B experiments comparing legacy-dot vs adapter-normalized-cosine on representative reranker workloads (NDCG, MRR)
Fuzz harness that randomizes vector norms and dimensions to catch edge-case numerical instability
CI job that runs regression tests on runtime-1.22 and flags changes to any scoring output for golden prompt sets
benchmarks: Canary p95 latency with normalization adapter: target <= 29ms
CPU overhead per 1k QPS for normalization pass: expected 1.8 cores on c5-large-equivalent; measure and optimize
Memory overhead for cached per-tenant norm-statistics: < 6MB per tenant on average
Quality: acceptable NDCG@10 delta <= 1.5% for existing customers when running compatibility mode
implementation_notes: Prefer streaming normalization (on-the-fly divide-by-norm) to avoid allocating large temporary buffers during batching
Cache per-tenant norm-distribution (mean, std, fraction of near-zero vectors) to allow 'auto' mode to pick sensible behavior
Expose an admin signal to mark a tenant as 'migrated' which changes default for that tenant to 'cosine' without client header
Ensure quantized kernels (int8/4) include an error bound evaluation for post-normalization; quantization might interact badly with tiny norms
Add a lightweight 'sanity' score check that refuses to return NaN/Inf and falls back to normalized-safe-value with an audit log
risks_and_tradeoffs: Defaulting to legacy-dot preserves existing customer quality but slows migration toward standard cosine semantics
On-the-fly normalization adds CPU overhead and slightly higher p95; must be mitigated with optimized vectorized kernels and selective application
Automatic detection (auto) risks misclassifying corpora with mixed-vector norms; will require conservative thresholds and manual overrides
Storing normalization state increases metadata surface area and must be included in backups/exports to prevent inconsistency after restore
Aggressive normalization on read can increase tail latency under heavy batching; fallback policies needed
comments: 2026-02-28 — Anika Shah: Kicked off spec PR. Primary constraint is avoiding client breakage while enabling predictable scoring semantics. Requested engineering estimate.
2026-03-03 — Marcus Lee: Implemented prototype normalization adapter in runtime branch 'embed-distance-shim'. Early microbenchmarks look ~3.2ms overhead p50, ~4.8ms p95 for a 512-d vector workload.
2026-03-05 — Priya Patel (PM): Requested clearer migration docs for customers with legacy vector stores; asked for export tool timeline.

2026-03-07 — Design review (internal): decided header name X-Embed-Similarity-Mode and SDK opt-in parameter 'similarity_mode' are acceptable. UX note: Console should show tenant mode on embeddings dashboard.

2026-03-10 — Marcus Lee: Hooked normalization adapter into batching layer with zero-copy when batch packing preserves alignment. Observed 7% higher throughput for aligned batches, but misaligned batches pay memory copy cost.
2026-03-12 — QA: Added fuzz tests for small-norm vectors and mixed-dimension payloads. Found numerical instability for vectors with norm < 1e-8; mitigation: clamp and log metric 'embed.norm.clamped'
2026-03-14 — Anika Shah: Approved canary gating metrics and scheduled 1% canary for Monday. Follow-ups: SDK release, docs, and dashboard card before canary start.
